body.estimand_functional: \((\widehat\theta,\widehat\tau_R)=(\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B,\ q^\top\{\widehat s_1-\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B\})\), with root-\(K\) influence \((\Phi_{\theta},\Phi_\tau)\)

sampling_model.design: A fixed set of target-pre, donor-pre, donor-post, and target factual-post cells is observed; treatment histories and grid times are fixed.
sampling_model.units: Each cell contains \(K\) independent individuals, and cell samples are mutually independent.
sampling_model.treatment: The target switches treatment after the pre period, while donor units remain under control; exact donor-span transport identifies the target's untreated post-period survival row.
sampling_model.overlap: Conditional censor survival is at least \(g>0\) through every required cell horizon.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting estimates conditional event and censor survival. Besides \(a_K\to0\), \(b_K\to0\), and \(a_Kb_K=o(K^{-1/2})\), the event learner is normalized at the follow-up origin, its relative-survival error path \(R_{cf}\) is almost surely of bounded variation, and \(\max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\). This variation condition is a substantive learner-class restriction, not a consequence of the ordinary product-rate assumption.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) impose event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, use a fixed-grid latent-factor/PCR transport, and form the spectral inputs from marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves; they do not derive covariate-adjusted AIPCW spectral influence inference.
Published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) gives asymptotic linearity for a directly estimated cross-fitted doubly robust treatment-specific survival curve.
Theorem 2 and Corollary 2 give row-space out-of-sample prediction guarantees for minimum-norm principal component regression.
Equation (4.12) gives the Fr\'echet derivative of the Moore--Penrose inverse under locally constant rank.
Sections 3--4 show interpolation, variance, and survival-curve bias for synthetic survival individuals.
Theorem 3.1 gives feasible inference for low-rank linear functionals when the working rank overestimates the true rank.

Theorem 2.1 recovers the factor space for bounded working rank at least the true rank as the cross-sectional dimension grows, and Theorem 3.2 with Corollary 3.1 gives over-estimated-rank-robust factor-augmented inference.

body.tldr: For fixed donor count, pre grid, post grid, rank, and a separated nonzero singular spectrum, covariate-adjusted cross-fitted AIPCW cell estimates admit a joint root-\(K\) expansion under censor positivity, a nuisance product rate, and explicit bounded-variation and variation-rate restrictions on the fitted relative-survival paths. Differentiating the target-pre, donor-pre, and donor-post blocks yields the full spectral influence vector, consistent covariance estimation, fixed-grid simultaneous bands, and a studentized grid-RMST interval. A matrix embedding shows that Han and Shah's unit-factor and time-factor spans imply the row-space and post-transport conditions used here, and the rational Kaplan--Meier/PCR bias witness lies in that fixed-grid factor subclass. Han and Shah already assume conditional independent censoring given treatment and covariates; the advance is covariate adjustment of their marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier step when covariate heterogeneity induces marginal dependent censoring. The weak-gap and selected-rank frontier remains open.

project_justification.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) already state event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, but their spectral workflow uses marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves and does not give a covariate-adjusted joint influence law. With heterogeneous covariates, conditional independence need not imply marginal independence, so those cell inputs can converge to distorted curves before PCR transport. Westling et al. (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4)) provide asymptotic-linearity theory for a directly estimated treatment-specific curve, not for a learned three-block spectral counterfactual.
project_justification.niche: With \(N_0,T_0,J,r\) fixed and \(K\to\infty\), the covariate-standardized cell curves form a finite-dimensional semiparametric first stage and the counterfactual is a smooth spectral functional only on a separated-rank neighborhood. The needed bridge combines an exact Stieltjes remainder under disclosed learner-path variation control, all three terms of the pseudoinverse derivative, and an algebraic embedding of Han--Shah's fixed-grid factor spans.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the repaired AIPCW cell expansion, the joint transported Gaussian law with consistently estimated influence vectors and covariance, a Gaussian-multiplier simultaneous band, and a studentized grid-RMST interval. It also proves a relatively open conditional-censoring subclass on which unadjusted marginal Kaplan--Meier/PCR has fixed bias, using an explicit rational witness that remains inside the Han--Shah factor/span subclass.

body.related_work: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) supply the fixed-grid latent-factor survival panel, unit and time spans, PCR transport, and the 925-patient, 10-country TCL application. They already assume event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates; the present advance is therefore not a weaker censoring premise, but replacement of marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier inputs by covariate-adjusted AIPCW inputs when within-cell covariate heterogeneity creates marginal dependent censoring, together with full transported inference. Proposition~\ref{prop:han-shah-fixed-grid-embedding} gives the exact matrix bridge from their spans to \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)\) and \(yM_r^+B\), while Proposition~\ref{prop:km-pcr-cancellation} certifies an open class of fixed Kaplan--Meier/PCR bias. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) and Sections 5.2--5.3) supply the cross-fitted augmented survival-score architecture and direct-curve asymptotic linearity, but not a data-dependent spectral transport. The relative-survival bounded-variation and variation-rate restrictions imposed here are additional primitive sufficient conditions not imposed by Westling et al., who instead assume the exact Stieltjes-remainder rate. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2) clarify minimum-norm PCR and row-space prediction without censoring-aware asymptotics. Golub and Pereyra (1973, equation (4.12)) are the matrix-calculus ancestor for the constant-rank pseudoinverse derivative. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024, Sections 3--4) analyze survival synthetic-control bias but do not derive this three-block PCR pseudo-limit or its relatively open nonzero-bias region. Fan and Liao (2022) and Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026) study growing-panel factor models or robustness to rank misspecification. Neither covers the fixed-donor, unregularized nonlinear pseudoinverse target under a local singular collision driven by orthogonal survival-score noise; accordingly, this note leaves weak-gap and rank-selection inference open.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theory is fixed-dimensional and, at the cell layer, applies only to event-survival learners whose relative-survival paths satisfy the stated bounded-variation and \(L_2\) variation-rate restrictions. Ordinary supremum or \(L_2\) consistency of survival ratios does not imply this property, so generic oscillatory learners are outside the theorem. The theory also does not cover a growing post grid, a shrinking singular gap, a selected rank, covariance degeneracy, or continuous-time RMST; the RMST target is exactly the fixed-grid functional \(q^\top(s_1-\theta)\).
body.honest_scope: The proved results cover only the fixed-panel, fixed-grid, exact-rank, fixed-singular-gap, exact-span, and exact-post-transport subclass. They additionally require within-cell i.i.d. sampling, independence of the samples across cells, conditional independent censoring, a common positive censor-survival bound, nondegenerate transported covariance, fixed-fold nuisance consistency and product rate, event-origin normalization, and the substantive bounded-variation and \(L_2\) variation-rate restrictions on fitted relative-survival paths. The joint-cell lemma is proved under those restrictions; the spectral limit, fixed-grid band, and grid-RMST interval inherit them transitively. The Han--Shah embedding is algebraic and supplies none of the within-cell sampling, cross-cell independence, censoring, covariance, or learner conditions. In particular, applying the theorem's standard errors or targeting interpretation to the 925-patient repeated-treatment-line TCL analysis requires those sampling and learner conditions to be verified for that application; the algebraic embedding alone does not verify cross-cell independence. The rational \(2\times2\) witness belongs to the fixed-grid factor/span subclass, while its negative Kaplan--Meier/PCR conclusion does not require the positive theorem's learner assumptions. Nothing here covers growing donor or time dimensions, a growing post grid, a shrinking or closed singular gap, selected rank, covariance degeneracy, approximate transport, or continuous-time RMST. The weak-gap and rank-selection problem remains the clear tier-changing follow-up, so the present contribution is a solid specialized fixed-grid result rather than a flagship general theory.
